_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2013: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2012 state of the verified 2012 register (China 4%, India's 7.5% end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection of 30 Oct 2012, the FOMC's 2% goal, the BoJ's 1% goal, New Zealand's 2012 PTA), plus the 2013 current-year targets set earlier (Türkiye 5%, set 21 Dec 2010 and kept 25 Dec 2012; Brazil 4.5%, CMN Res. 3,991 of 30 Jun 2011; Colombia 3% ±1, Board of 23 Nov 2012; Indonesia 4.5% ±1, PMK 66/PMK.011/2012 of 30 Apr 2012; Korea 2.5–3.5% for the three years from 2013, MPC of 11 Oct 2012), and the changes announced during 2013: the BoJ's 2% 'price stability target' (22 Jan), China's annual objective (5 Mar), the RBI's end-of-fiscal-year WPI figures (29 Jan review: 6.8% for March 2013; 3 May Annual Policy: 'a level of 5.0 per cent' by the end of the fiscal year, kept on 30 Jul; the reviews of 20 Sep, 29 Oct and 18 Dec state no numeric end-March figure, so 5.0 stays the last stated one), and the RBA's new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy (24 Oct), recorded although the value is unchanged because it replaces the row's wording. The UK remit of 20 Mar 2013 re-confirms 2% CPI (value and wording unchanged, not recorded); Thailand's 2013 core-inflation target (0.5–3.0%, reported in the BoT's January 2013 Monetary Policy Report) equals 2012's and is not recorded. Every new source URL was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no page names a later year.
note: Three economies had no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve's statements refer to the PCE price index (see its row; the benchmark is applied to headline CPI), the RBI's objectives referred to the wholesale price index (the benchmark is the RBI's stated end-of-fiscal-year WPI figure), and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, 25 Jan 2012: 'The Committee judges that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate.'
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy, 25 Jan 2012

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'The Price Stability Goal in the Medium to Long Term', 14 Feb 2012: the goal 'is in a positive range of 2 percent or lower in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI) and, more specifically, set a goal at 1 percent for the time being' (replacing the 'understanding of medium- to long-term price stability').

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The Price Stability Goal in the Medium to Long Term, 14 Feb 2012

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada, 8 Nov 2011: 'The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement was renewed for another five-year period.

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 8 Nov 2011

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 30 Sep 2010: 'keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 30 Sep 2010

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2007:3, October 2007
Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Policy Targets Agreement signed 20 Sep 2012: 'The agreement continues to require the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term. Within this target, the new agreement now requires the Bank to focus on keeping future average inflation near 2 per cent.'

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'New Policy Targets Agreement signed today', 20 Sep 2012 (Scoop)

CN.wording: Government Work Report delivered 5 Mar 2012: 'Consumer Price Index (CPI) increase will be kept around 4 percent' this year (a government objective, not a PBoC target; 2011's was also around 4%).

urls.label: Beijing Review, 'Highlights: Premier Wen's Government Work Report', 5 Mar 2012

IN.wording: RBI Second Quarter Review for 2012–13: 'the baseline projection for headline WPI inflation for March … is raised to 7.5 per cent from 7.0 per cent indicated in July' (end of fiscal year 2012–13; wholesale price index; no CPI target).
IN.index: WPI; benchmark applied to the CPI series used here

urls.label: RBI Second Quarter Review of Monetary Policy 2012–13, 30 Oct 2012 (para 38)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2013, 25 Dec 2012

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007

CZ.wording: 'The CNB announces the new inflation target as annual consumer price index growth of 2% (with a tolerance band of ± 1%), effective from January 2010'.

CNB press release, 'The CNB issues Inflation Report I/2010', 12 Feb 2010 (the new inflation target of 2%)

KR.wording: Inflation target for 2013 onwards set by the Monetary Policy Committee on 11 Oct 2012: 'the range between 2.5 and 3.5 percent, in terms of the rate of change in the consumer price index', applied over three years (midpoint 3.0%).

urls.label: Bank of Korea, 'Inflation Target for 2013 onwards', 11 Oct 2012

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'
